project.name: test
project.seedPrompt:
Product objective
Build a lightweight, general-purpose test application that validates the end-to-end Fish Bowl project creation and deployment pipeline. The application must compile, pass linting and tests, and deploy successfully to Vercel on every push to the main branch. It serves as a proving ground for scaffold integrity, CI/CD confidence, and iterative feature development.

Target users and jobs-to-be-done
Primary users are the internal engineering and product teams evaluating Fish Bowl's create-project workflow. Their core job is to confirm that a newly provisioned project boots correctly, renders a functional page, and accepts incremental feature additions without regressions. Secondary users are downstream authoring agents that will extend the scaffold with product-specific features.

Value proposition
This project provides a verified, deployment-ready baseline that eliminates guesswork about whether the scaffold, build toolchain, and hosting integration are working. Teams can confidently layer features on top knowing the foundation is sound.

Scope for next iterations
The immediate next iteration should introduce a simple interactive element—such as a form input, toggle, or counter—to exercise client-side state and demonstrate that React hydration works correctly in the deployed environment. Following that, add a server action or API route to validate full-stack data flow. Each iteration should include corresponding test coverage.

Non-goals
Do not implement authentication, database integrations, payment processing, or third-party API consumption at this stage. Do not add complex state management libraries or routing beyond what Next.js App Router provides out of the box. Avoid premature optimization or performance tuning.

Product and implementation guardrails
All code must pass yarn lint with zero warnings, yarn test with all tests passing, and yarn build with no errors before merging to main. Use only the dependencies already present in the scaffold unless a capability request has been approved in capabilities.md. Follow the visual direction in .fish-bowl/style.md and consume tokens from .fish-bowl/style.tokens.json for all UI decisions. Keep components small, typed, and testable. Do not introduce runtime environment variables without documenting them.

Commercial success signals
Successful project creation and first deployment without manual intervention. Zero lint or build errors across the first five feature iterations. Downstream agents can extend the project without requiring scaffold modifications. Deployment previews generate on every pull request and production deploys complete within two minutes.

Near-term roadmap direction
Phase 1: Validate scaffold integrity (current). Phase 2: Add a simple interactive UI component with tests. Phase 3: Introduce a server action or API route demonstrating full-stack capability. Phase 4: Integrate style tokens into component theming for visual consistency. Phase 5: Establish a pattern library of reusable UI primitives for downstream agent consumption.
